Kalendár Seznam.cz podporuje protokol CalDAV, takže by malo byť možné pripojiť ho aj k programu Mozilla Thunderbird. Problém môže byť v adrese servera, prihlasovaní alebo automatickom vyhľadávaní kalendárov.

Podľa dostupných technických informácií používa Seznam.cz server https://caldav.seznam.cz.

1. Skúste nasledujúci postup

  • Otvorte Thunderbird.
  • Prejdite do časti Kalendár.
  • Kliknite pravým tlačidlom myši na zoznam kalendárov.
  • Vyberte Nový kalendár.
  • Zvoľte V sieti.
  • Do poľa Používateľské meno zadajte svoju úplnú e-mailovú adresu na Seznam.cz.

Do poľa Adresa zadajte: https://caldav.seznam.cz

Nezaškrtávajte možnosť „Toto umiestnenie nevyžaduje prihlasovacie údaje“. Kliknite na Nájsť kalendáre. Ak Thunderbird požiada o heslo, zadajte prihlasovacie heslo k účtu Seznam.cz.

Tento postup zodpovedá spôsobu pridávania sieťových kalendárov v Thunderbirde.

2. Ak Thunderbird kalendár nenájde Vyskúšajte alternatívnu adresu: https://caldav.seznam.cz/.well-known/caldav Ide o štandardnú cestu používanú pri vyhľadávaní kalendárov CalDAV. Nie je však zaručené, že ju Thunderbird prijme ako adresu kalendára.

content:
Certificate problems can be caused by a number of reasons, including:

- Incorrect server settings – especially connection security or server mismatch. Confirm that your server settings are correct. Here are Windstream's recommended settings:

https://www.gokinetic.com/support/my-account/email-101/what-server-settings-do-i-use-for-windstream-email

- Antivirus or Proxy – it can modify certificates with its own and interfere with connection security. As a test, disable them or create an exception for Thunderbird.

- Expired Certificate – due to incorrect date & time or genuine expiration. This would be only correctable by Windstream. They may already be aware of it and are working on a fix, so if you just wait a while the problem may go away. It might be worth a call to them to report the problem and get a status update.

Your actual Thunderbird start page is displaying the Account Hub "Add your email address". This means that Thunderbird has created a new profile and is prompting the user to create an email account. Thunderbird does not open your old profile since obviously there is no "connection" between the Thunderbird application and your old profile folder.

Restart Thunderbird and click on the little "Minimize" ⟳ symbol to close the account hub. Click the app menu button ≡ then Help > Troubleshooting Information > Profile Folder > Open Folder..., then quit Thunderbird. Now in Windows Explorer you will see a folder named "xxxxxxxx.default-release" (or similar name) which is the new (virgin) profile folder. From the profile folder go up one level in the folder "Profiles" and make a screen shot of its contents. Go um one more level in the folder "Thunderbird" where you'll see a file "profiles.ini" Open profiles.ini in a text editor and do a screen shot of its contents.

content:
re :AOL requires 2 factor authorisation,

It only requires it because you selected it. If you did not use third party email clients and only accessed AOL via webmail account using a browser then I would advise 2 step verification.

Access the webmail account and switch 2FA off. Depending upon which server you are using to access the AOL account, it requires different password set up.

Are you using the Incoming mail server (IMAP): imap.aol.com server setting ? If yes: Recent changes mean third party apps require you to create/generate a special app password. This is what AOL say on their website. If you use a 3rd-party email app to access your AOL Mail account, you may need a special code to give that app permission to access your AOL account. Please read Info:

  • https://help.aol.com/articles/create-and-manage-app-password

Have you logged on to the webmail account and created/generated 'an app password' just to use in Thunderbird? If not, then logon to webmail account, disable/switch off 2FA and then generate the special app password which you can only use in Thunderbird. Use the special generated app password in Thunderbird instead of normal password.


Are you using the Yahoo server to access AOL account ? If yes, then you would be using 'Authentication Method' = Oauth Please read this info:

  • https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/thunderbird-and-yahoo

Use the 'normal password' (not an app generated password) when setting up account and granting Thunderbird access to the account which will then create the oauth token and save it in the stored passwords. Thunderbird will use that oauth token to get access.
